answer: Give each agent identity weight through vested reputation payouts: new agents earn rewards only if they keep contributing across many epochs, and payments vest gradually, so a flash-farmed account that spirals in and out forfeits most of its earnings when it exits early. An attacker spawning thousands of violet-ringed sybil identities must therefore lock real work and time into each one, while the grove of long-lived agents compounds trust that newcomers cannot fake cheaply. The cost per fake identity approaches the value of genuine participation, collapsing the economics of mass attacks.
